questions.question: Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. It is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Raja Parba is a three-day-long festival celebrated in Odisha. It honors Mother Earth (Bhudevi) during her menstruation, symbolizing the onset of the monsoon and the fertility of the soil.

Note: During these days, all agricultural work stops, and people celebrate with traditional swings (Doli) and pithas (cakes).

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated for fertility and better fortune in Jharkhand?
questions.solution:
The Jawa festival is celebrated in Jharkhand primarily by unmarried tribal girls for fertility and better fortune.

Ritual: Girls decorate a basket with germinating seeds of grains like barley, wheat, and maize, which is central to the dance and songs performed during the celebration.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is called the month of merits and is celebrated between May and June?
questions.solution:
Saga Dawa is known as the 'Month of Merits' in Sikkim. It is the most sacred festival for Buddhists, commemorating the birth, enlightenment, and Parinirvana (death) of Lord Buddha.

Timing: It typically falls on the full moon day of the fourth month of the Tibetan lunar calendar (May/June).

questions.question: Which of the following Hindu festivals is celebrated in the last month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:
Holi, the festival of colors, is celebrated on the Purnima (full moon) of the month of Phalguna, which is the last month of the Hindu calendar.

Context: This marks the end of winter and the arrival of spring, followed immediately by the Hindu New Year in the month of Chaitra.

questions.question: The ‘Hornbill Festival’ is a celebration held every year from 1 to 10 December in ______.
questions.solution:
The Hornbill Festival, often called the 'Festival of Festivals', is organized by the State Tourism Department of Nagaland every year from December 1 to 10.

Purpose: It aims to revive and protect the rich culture of Nagaland and display its traditional extravaganzas and tribal heritage at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama.

questions.question: Arthunkal Feast and Vettukad Festival are church festivals from the state of ______.
questions.solution:
The Arthunkal Feast (St. Sebastian's Feast) and Vettukad Festival (Feast of Christ the King) are significant church festivals from Kerala.

Note: St. Andrew's Basilica at Arthunkal is one of the most famous shrines in India, attracting pilgrims of all faiths.

questions.question: ‘Ugadi’ is the famous festival of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Ugadi is the New Year's Day for the people of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.

Ritual: A special dish called Ugadi Pachadi is prepared, which combines six different tastes representing the various emotions of life (happiness, sadness, anger, fear, disgust, and surprise).

questions.question: Shigmotsav is essentially a festival of the masses, celebrated on the full moon day in the month of Phalguna (March). Which state celebrates this festival?
questions.solution:
Shigmotsav (or Shigmo) is the spring festival celebrated in Goa. It is the Goan counterpart of Holi and features grand street parades with folk dances like Ghode Modni and Fugdi.

Timing: It is celebrated over 14 days, ending on the full moon of the month of Phalguna.

questions.question: In which of the following neighbouring countries of India is the famous Katas Raj Temples complex, with shrines of multiple faiths, located?
questions.solution:
The Katas Raj Temples complex is located in the Chakwal District of Pakistan. It is a sacred site for Hindus, centered around a pond that, according to legend, was created from the teardrops of Lord Shiva.

Note: The site also houses remains of Buddhist stupas and ancient havelis.

questions.question: How many monasteries and temples are there in Ellora caves?
questions.solution:
The Ellora Caves in Maharashtra consist of 34 monasteries and temples carved side-by-side into the wall of a high basalt cliff.

Composition: The complex includes 12 Buddhist (caves 1–12), 17 Hindu (caves 13–29), and 5 Jain (caves 30–34) monuments, showcasing the religious harmony of ancient India.

questions.question: Hoysaleswara Temple is located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Hoysaleswara Temple, a 12th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, is located in Halebidu, Karnataka.

Architecture: It is a masterpiece of Hoysala architecture, famous for its intricate soapstone carvings and its 'double' temple structure (Dvikuta).

questions.question: In which of the following states is Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple located?
questions.solution:
The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple is a famous pilgrimage site dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, located in the Perunad Grama Panchayat of Pathanamthitta district, Kerala.

Location: It is situated atop a hill in the Periyar Tiger Reserve and is one of the largest annual pilgrimage sites in the world.

questions.question: Where is Kandariya Mahadev Temple situated?
questions.solution:
The Kandariya Mahadev Temple is the largest and most ornate Hindu temple in the Khajuraho Group of Monuments in Madhya Pradesh.

Significance: Built by the Chandela rulers, it is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its Nagara-style architecture.

questions.question: Where is Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) situated?
questions.solution:
Sri Harmandir Sahib, popularly known as the Golden Temple, is the preeminent spiritual site of Sikhism, located in the city of Amritsar, Punjab.

History: The Amrit Sarovar (tank) was excavated by Guru Ram Das, and the temple's foundation was laid by the Sufi saint Mian Mir.

questions.question: In which of the following states is Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Temple located?
questions.solution:
Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Temple is located at Srisailam in Andhra Pradesh.

Unique Fact: It is one of the rare temples in India that is considered both a Jyotirlinga (dedicated to Lord Shiva) and a Shakti Peetha (dedicated to Goddess Parvati/Bhramaramba).
